title: Compand with mu-law and write a WAV file
brief: Build 8-bit mu-law encoding and decoding, convert floats to 16-bit PCM, and write and read WAV files with struct so the bytes match Python's wave module.
hints: np.log1p(mu * np.abs(x)) is ln(1 + mu |x|), and it stays accurate for tiny x.
Map F(x) from [-1, 1] to [0, mu] with np.floor((y + 1) / 2 * mu + 0.5), and invert it with y = 2 * codes / mu - 1.
Clip before astype(np.int16): 1.0 times 32768 is 32768, which wraps to -32768 without the clip.
struct.pack('<HHIIHH', 1, channels, rate, rate * 2 * channels, 2 * channels, 16) is the whole 16-byte fmt body.
An int16 array shaped (frames, channels) is already in interleaved order: pcm.astype('<i2').tobytes() writes L0 R0 L1 R1 and so on.
When walking chunks, advance by 8 + size, plus 1 more when size is odd.
